overall: Atlanta is starting the day under a fully overcast sky (OVC, ceiling ~122m/400ft) with temperatures remarkably flat near 73.4°F since midnight — an unusual pattern for late June that suggests a stubborn stratus or fog layer suppressing the normal overnight-into-morning warming. The 30-minute velocity of +3.6°F/hr hints that some warming is beginning, but the 2-hour velocity of only +0.9°F/hr confirms the broader trend remains sluggish. If the cloud deck breaks as the NWS 'mostly sunny' narrative implies, heating could accelerate sharply through the early-to-mid afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster in a tighter band (HRRR=83.4°F, ECMWF=85.5°F, NBM=86.4°F) and sit meaningfully below the NWS text high of 88°F, suggesting the official forecast may be slightly optimistic. Model spread is modest (~3°F), but the HRRR — the most cloud-aware short-range model — is the most conservative, likely reflecting the persistent overcast. The ensemble abort signals ('no_trade', Tier 4, entropy ~2.4-2.5) confirm that distributional uncertainty is high and no single bucket dominates.
max_temp_prediction: The critical driver today is when — or whether — the overcast breaks. With a running max of only 73.4°F at 09:50 ET and peak timing expected around 14-15h ET, temperatures need to climb roughly 12-15°F in 4-5 hours; that is achievable only with meaningful sunshine. The META model's highest probability sits at 84-85°F (25.1%), with secondary mass at 86-87°F and 88-89°F (both 22.1%), pointing to a central estimate around 85-86°F. Weighting that against NWP consensus (~85°F) and the cloud-suppression risk if clearing is delayed, confidence is moderate-low; the realistic range spans roughly 83-88°F, with a best-estimate lean toward the ECMWF value.
